tagline: Two lakes of different making, and ducks that walk on fish.
intro: The byway strings US 6, PA 18, PA 618 and PA 285 together through the rural west end of Crawford County, past two lakes of very different making.

Pymatuning was a great swamp, where farm animals that wandered off were lost in the quicksand, until about 7,000 men went to work damming the Shenango River in 1931 and made a lake 17 miles long. Conneaut Lake is the glaciers' work, a kettle lake left where a block of ice broke off the retreating front and melted in place. By surface area it is the largest natural lake in Pennsylvania.

moments.title: Linesville
moments.text: At the town's one traffic light a sign on the Maclaine Building puts Chicago and New York each 500 miles off, though the true halfway point is about a mile west.

moments.title: Linesville Spillway
moments.text: South of town in warm weather the carp crowd the spillway so thick that ducks walk across their backs, billed locally as Pennsylvania's second most popular attraction, after the Liberty Bell.

moments.title: Conneaut Lake
moments.text: The lake was raised about ten feet in the 1820s for the Beaver and Erie Canal, then let back down to its natural level once the railroads had made canals obsolete.
